Subject: RFI: security segmentation + maintenance windows (follow-up)

Hi Jasmine / Monica,

Thanks for the RFI packet — we've had the security team review Appendix A and had a couple of follow-ups specifically around maintenance windows, planned downtime notifications, and how your segregated environments are affected during kernel/firmware updates. Our external assessor (ForgeSec) also flagged a place where the BAA redline might require language around scheduled maintenance and PHI access during those windows.

Can you confirm: 1) typical maintenance window cadence for Dedicated clusters, 2) whether you provide pre-announced time-of-day windows (UTC/local), and 3) whether there is an automated rollback policy that prevents partial state where PHI could be exposed?

We're trying to scope a pass/fail item for our compliance board that meets our legal team's BAA language. Attached are the sections they marked in our draft BAA.

Thanks — Priya

Subject: Re: RFI: security segmentation + maintenance windows (follow-up)

Hi Priya — thanks for the clear notes and for sharing the redline. Looping Markus for the technical details. Quick summary answers up front:

- Maintenance cadence (Dedicated): customers can choose a weekly, biweekly, or monthly scheduled maintenance window for non-emergency platform-level updates; for security patches critical to CVSS >= 7.0 we occasionally perform out-of-band updates with prior notice.
- Window scheduling: we support customer-specified windows in UTC or local time and push reminders 72/24 hours before the window; emergency patches get a 4–24 hour heads-up when possible.
- Rollback/PHI safety: our Dedicated runtime applies atomic orchestration steps: KV cache checkpointing, write-quiesce to persistent storage, and a pre-flight validation that prevents partial schema migrations. If any step fails we abort and roll back to the last known-good snapshot — PHI access is disabled to end-users during snapshot churn.

Markus, can you add the technical artifact references we promised (network diagram, maintenance policy CSV, and a note on how KMS/HSM keys are handled during node maintenance)?

Best,
Jasmine

Hi Priya, team — adding the technical details you can reference in the RFI: see attached network_diagram_v2.png and maintenance_policy_summary.csv. Short technical clarifications: 

1) Isolation during maintenance: Dedicated customer pools run in tenant-specific namespaces; control plane operations operate through per-tenant service accounts restricted by mTLS and RBAC. During node updates we drain user-facing processes into a warm standby instance before kernel/driver patching — no live PHI transactions touch nodes under update.

2) KMS/HSM handling: Customer keys (for Private and Dedicated) remain in the customer Vault/HSM; for Hosted we offer a customer-managed KMS option (BYOK) and a Redwood-managed KMS with HSM-backed keys. During maintenance, key service endpoints are not rotated; we rotate session tokens and re-encrypt ephemeral caches only after successful node reintegration. Key material never leaves HSM.

3) Audit trails & evidence: every maintenance run generates an immutable audit bundle (operation ID + timestamps + operator id) that we can export as a limited-access evidence package for auditors. We maintain these logs for 13 months by default; retention can be extended via an add-on.

Attachments: network_diagram_v2.png, maintenance_policy_summary.csv

We'll aim to complete the RFI review by next Tuesday if we can get the failure-mode and maintenance cap confirmed.

Subject: Re: RFI: security segmentation + maintenance windows (follow-up)

Hi Priya — quick answers inline and an action list so we can close your control annex: 

1) Failure-mode deterministic description (for your annex): 
- Step 1: Orchestration pauses at node-drain checkpoint; flags set: maintenance_in_progress=true, drain_success=true/false.
- Step 2: If a pre-flight health check fails, orchestration sets abort_reason=preflight_failed, triggers rehydration from last snapshot, and sets maintenance_state=rollback_initiated.
- Step 3: System blocks all uncommitted write transactions; maintenance_state moves to rollback_completed once snapshot reattach succeeds; maintenance_in_progress=false and operation_id is logged for audit.

2) Maintenance cap: Redwood can commit to a default 6-hour cap for customer-designated scheduled windows on Dedicated and Private deployments. Emergency patches are outside the cap but we will provide a documented emergency notification process and post-incident evidence. We will add the 6-hour language to the BAA redline if that works for your legal team.

3) Hosted KMS options: for Hosted customers we support BYOK into major cloud KMS services (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault) and we also support HSM-on-prem connectors via a secure tunnel for customers who require their own HSM backing. We will document connector requirements and the supported HSM models in the evidence pack.

Next steps/action owners: 
- Markus: finalize a one-page failure-mode snippet and add to RFI Appendix A (by 2027-09-24).
- Jasmine / Sales: confirm BAA redline update and share DocuSign link for sign-off (by 2027-09-24).
- Monica: prepare hosted-KMS connector spec and sample config (by 2027-09-27).

If these timelines work we'll aim to return the completed evidence pack and revised BAA by the end of next week.

Thanks — Monica
